prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project and Google Account
prerequisites.detail: Enable the Gmail API in the API Library and create a Web application OAuth client.

prerequisites.title: Public domain with home page and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Home page must be public and the privacy policy hosted on the same domain and linked from the consent screen. Authorized domains need ownership verified in Search Console.

prerequisites.title: Billing enabled for Marketplace publishing
prerequisites.detail: Enable billing in your Google Cloud project before publishing to the Marketplace.

steps.title: Prototype with Composio managed Gmail app
steps.detail: Use the managed app to build and test the agent; no OAuth app needed.
steps.done_when: Agent can call Gmail tools on a test account

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Prefer non-sensitive scopes; ask for restricted ones only if needed. Draft scope justifications.

steps.title: Create Cloud project, consent screen, OAuth client
steps.detail: Configure Branding, Audience and Data Access, then create a Web application client. Save the client secret immediately; it is shown once.

steps.title: Add Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Google client; it must match exactly and use HTTPS. Google verifies authorized domains, and the developer cannot verify Composio's callback domain, so proxy the callback through your own domain.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Verify and publish branding
steps.detail: Verify authorized domains, then click Verify Branding and Publish branding within 7 days.

steps.title: Record demo video
steps.detail: Show the OAuth grant flow in English, the consent screen with client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use. Upload to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Submit data access verification
steps.detail: Enter justifications and submit in the OAuth Verification Center.

steps.title: Wait for Google verification
steps.detail: Google may email for more information.

steps.title: Book security assessment (restricted scopes)
steps.detail: Required for restricted scope data stored or transmitted on servers. Start early.

steps.title: Submit Marketplace listing for review
steps.detail: Create the listing and submit once OAuth verification is done.

traps.title: Security assessment starts too late
traps.detail: Reports say it takes weeks, and a missed deadline made one developer's verification lapse. An existing pentest is reported not to count; only an authorized lab letter is accepted.

traps.title: Testing mode limits
traps.detail: Testing apps are capped at 100 test users and have refresh tokens that expire after 7 days. Unverified published apps with sensitive scopes are also capped at 100 users.

traps.title: Extra OAuth clients slow review
traps.detail: A community report says extra clients in one project can trigger demo video requests for each; delete unused clients.

traps.title: Branding cannot change during verification
traps.detail: You must cancel verification to edit branding. Compliant brand results expire after 7 days if unpublished.

traps.title: Wrong consent screen setup fails Marketplace review
traps.detail: Internal user type, Testing status, or incomplete OAuth verification are common reasons for failure.

traps.title: Audience choice is permanent
traps.detail: After publishing a Marketplace app as public or private, you cannot change it.

blockers.symptom: Unverified app screen shown to users
blockers.what_it_means: The app is not verified for the scopes it requests.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit a verification request, or limit use to known test users.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft scope justifications and a demo video script.

blockers.what_it_means: The redirect URI sent does not exactly match an authorized one.
blockers.what_to_do: Copy the exact URI from the Composio dashboard, including scheme and trailing slash.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the two URIs and flag differences.

blockers.symptom: Workspace users cannot authorize the app
blockers.what_it_means: The customer's admin may have blocked or restricted the app or its scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer admin to allow or trust your OAuth client ID.
blockers.agent_can_help: Write an admin instruction note with the client ID.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Based on FAQs, if your project contains multiple OAuth clients, Google needs videos demonstrating usage of restricted scopes for each of those clients. Failure to do so might be resulting in multiple communications.
evidence.answer: Community answer (2019, dated): extra OAuth clients in one project can trigger requests for restricted-scope demo videos for each client, causing repeated communications; removing unused clients may help.
